2190.title: SQLite db silently reverted to a 2-week-old state while the server was running (post-Aug-9 projects/threads lost; auto-update in progress)
2190.rootCauseOneLine: bb keeps the entire database in bb.db-wal (WAL mode, SQLite's default 1000-page auto-checkpoint only, handle never closed at shutdown), so bb.db can be weeks stale or empty and any pinned reader freezes it; when the WAL header/wal-index becomes unreadable SQLite recovery silently treats the WAL as empty and the still-open server handle serves the last checkpoint. The reporter's bb.db mtime at 15:10 is NOT produced by this mechanism (the post-revert commit does not write bb.db; bb would need ~1000 more WAL pages), so an external actor that wrote bb.db directly (in-place restore/copy/sync of the three files) is now the leading candidate; it was not identified.
2190.proposedFix: (1) Close the SQLite handle in runShutdown() (apps/server/src/start-server.ts) so SQLite performs its close-time checkpoint — bounds the empty-bb.db exposure across restarts, does not help the reporter's no-restart/pinned case; (2) periodic PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) (e.g. every 60 s in the sweeps) that reads (busy, log, checkpointed) and logs a warning when checkpointed < log repeatedly ("a reader is pinning bb.db-wal; bb.db is N frames behind") plus WAL size — bounds the window only when no reader pins the WAL (pinned-reader experiment shows checkpointed:0 of 8314 while pinned), otherwise its value is the warning; (3) a went-backwards tripwire: persist a monotonic high-water mark (e.g. MAX(events.sequence)) to a sidecar file each sweep and, if the live DB is ever below it, log an error, surface it in UI/CLI and stop checkpointing so stale WAL frames (recoverable with issue-2190-wal-tool.mjs recover) are not overwritten — mitigates every candidate including an external rewrite; (4) daily VACUUM INTO rolling backups with small retention — the only item that restores data under every candidate; (5) document that in-process plugins must never open bb.db* with fs APIs (POSIX lock drop). Tests: the packages/db test cannot observe a server-level fix; add apps/server tests that boot against a temp data dir, write, run shutdown and assert the main file alone holds the row; that a pinned reader produces the warning; and that the tripwire fires.
2190.caveats: Revision addressed all verifier findings by re-running: (a) the harness-only wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) was removed from walkthrough step 6 (now prints 'bb.db mtime changed: false'), and new steps 9-10 measure that bb on its own needs 195 one-row commits (1001 WAL pages) before the auto-checkpoint writes bb.db, by which point stale frames are overwritten and recovery is impossible; an explicitly labelled induced checkpoint is the only thing that changes the mtime. The mtime claim row is now 'Not explained by the simulated mechanism' and 5.3 re-ranks candidates, noting a SQLite checkpoint cannot both write bb.db and lose data, so an in-place rewrite of the three files by a non-SQLite actor is now ranked first. (b) Pinned-reader script now issues an explicit PASSIVE checkpoint while pinned: {"busy":0,"log":8314,"checkpointed":0}; section 6 states per candidate what each fix mitigates. (c) Section 4E and the test docblock no longer claim the packages/db test guards a server-level fix; the test now asserts the post-revert commit leaves bb.db mtime unchanged (3/3 pass on fcada5a3b). (d) Part A is fully derived (DATA from bb-dev-app status, host id from /api/v1/hosts, scratch repo created) and was re-run on a fresh instance (ports 16667/24667/32667) with the verbatim transcript attached; this time the post-SIGTERM capture preceded the supervisor restart. (e) Minor corrections: identical better-sqlite3 12.10.0 / SQLite 3.53.1 pin as desktop-v0.38.0, 'same salt' comment, 'recreated data survived' row now Unverified (mechanism consistent). The spontaneous trigger remains unreproduced; the reporter's cold copy inspected with issue-2190-wal-tool.mjs is decisive. Issue Type/Effort metadata still unreadable (token lacks read:project). Cleanup done: pnpm dev:stop, leftover pids killed, data dir deleted, ports 16667/24667/32667 confirmed free, copied test files removed from the worktree (git status clean).

2166.title: automation update writes an over-cap prompt despite rejecting it, then no read of that project's automations succeeds
2166.rootCauseOneLine: The `bb automation` CLI handler hands its hand-built request to the plugin service without the Zod request-schema parse the RPC route applies; the service commits the row and only then serializes it through automationExecutionSchema (which carries the 8000-char cap), and that same capped schema decodes every stored row on list/show/update/sweep, so the over-cap row becomes unreadable and unrepairable.
2166.proposedFix: Two changes in plugins/automations (prototyped in repro/prototype-fix.diff; repro desired-behaviour tests pass, all 78 existing plugin tests and typecheck stay green): (1) validate at the argv boundary like the RPC route does: in cli.ts return agentExecutionUpdateSchema.parse(update) from buildAgentExecutionUpdate and parse the agent branch of buildExecution with an exported agent-only request schema carrying the .max(AUTOMATION_PROMPT_MAX_LENGTH) cap (do NOT parse the whole request with updateAutomationInputSchema: the CLI's --script-file shape sends both script and scriptFile and would be rejected, breaking three existing tests); (2) separate request policy from stored/response shape: drop .max() from automationAgentExecutionSchema.prompt and automationScriptExecutionSchema.script (used by parseAutomationExecution and automationResponseSchema) and re-apply the caps only in automationExecutionRequestSchema and agentExecutionUpdateSchema, so existing over-cap rows become readable, listable and repairable with a plain `bb automation update --prompt` and affected users recover by upgrading. Optional: per-row try/catch in service.list (as overview already does) and human-readable ZodError formatting in the CLI. No wire shape changes, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
2166.caveats: One issue claim is refuted: the corrupted automation does NOT keep running on schedule. The sweep parses the stored row with the same schema, logs `Skipping due automation <id> with invalid stored configuration` at ERROR every 10 s, never claims or advances it (run_count 0, automation_runs empty), verified live and by unit test; scheduler code is identical between desktop-v0.39.0 and the base commit. What is true is that the app overview silently drops the row (WARN only), so the UI shows no trace. Also found that `bb automation create --prompt <over-cap>` has the same insert-then-reject defect, and the inline --script 262144 cap has the same failure mode. No real provider turn was run (the healthy automation was paused). The prototype diff was reverted; the worktree only retains plugins/automations/src/issue-2166.test.ts.

2160.title: Pi keeps using previous model after model picker change until /compact
2160.rootCauseOneLine: Since the bridge-protocol migration (c5b53caab, #1640) the runtime never diffs execution options and expects each bridge to reconcile them per turn, but the Pi bridge only reads options.model/reasoningLevel at session construction (thread/start|resume|fork); handleTurnStart ignores params.options, so AgentSession.setModel is never called and every later turn and compaction runs on the construction model until something rebuilds the session (thread/resume).
2160.proposedFix: In packages/agent-runtime/src/pi/bridge: add PiSdkSession.applyTurnOptions({model, thinkingLevel}) that resolves options.model via resolveConfiguredModel(session.modelRuntime, ...) and applies it to the live AgentSession when it differs from session.model (plus setThinkingLevel for reasoningLevel), and call it at the top of handleTurnStart (before both the /compact and prompt branches) and handleTurnSteer, failing the turn with a clear error if resolution fails. Prototype patch (2160/repro/prototype-fix.patch) applies cleanly to fcada5a3b, makes both failing repro tests pass, keeps the 11 pre-existing Pi suites (147 tests; 12/149 with the repro file) green and `turbo run typecheck --filter=@bb/agent-runtime --force` green. Caveat for the real PR: AgentSession.setModel/setThinkingLevel also persist defaultProvider/defaultModel/defaultThinkingLevel into the user's global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, which session construction does not do today; use the lower-level pieces (modelRuntime.checkAuth + session.agent.state.model + sessionManager.appendModelChange + re-clamp thinking level) or an upstream non-persisting setter. Add a bridge test (and ideally a conformance rule) that sends turn/start with different options than thread/start. No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed.
2160.caveats: (1) Revision: fixed the major finding for real, not just in prose. All helper scripts (wait-idle.sh, tell-file.sh, bb-turn-models.py) now read $BB_SERVER_URL from `eval "$(scripts/bb-dev-app env)"` (or an explicit argument) with nothing hardcoded; tell-file.sh takes <thread> <model> <file>; new make-filler.sh generates the filler. I then re-ran the entire live repro from scratch on a fresh dev instance (:15047/:23047/:31047, thread thr_ahgjgq8fc9) using exactly the commands now printed in section 4a; the output shown is from that run: tell with grok-4.6 answered by gpt-5-mini (in=106), real compaction (tokensBefore=47429) followed by another stale gpt-5-mini turn, and thread stop + new turn switching to grok-4.6 after thread/identity seq 51. Minor findings fixed: test counts corrected to 11 suites/147 tests pre-existing (12/149 with the repro file, re-measured), and the 4-minute hang is now marked as a non-reproducible one-off (the re-run's stop/resume took ~6 s) and kept only in the caveats. Added section 10 "Verification" describing the verifier's run and what changed. (2) pi-assistant-models.txt and bb-turn-models.txt were overwritten in place with the revised run; the original run remains fully recoverable from pi-session-thr_iyyz7w3cxf.jsonl and thread-events-final.json (kept, not moved). (3) The issue's '/compact resyncs it' claim is refuted three times now (author x2, verifier x1). (4) Live repro still switches between two github-copilot models rather than cross-provider (anthropic/openai-codex OAuth failed on this machine in the original run; not retried); the code path is identical. (5) Prototype fix validated by unit tests + typecheck only, not live, because Pi's setModel would write the user's global Pi settings. (6) Post-compaction input tokens do not drop because the single ~42k-token filler message exceeds keepRecentTokens and is kept whole; the compaction entry and thread/compacted event are real. (7) Cleanup done: dev instance stopped, data dir ~/.bb-dev/...wf_21e66a79-f02-13-8d26b48f1e80 deleted, /tmp/bb-2160-qa and scratch scripts removed, my Pi session file thr_ahgjgq8fc9.jsonl removed from ~/.bb/pi-bridge-sessions, ports 15047/23047/31047 confirmed free, worktree restored clean at fcada5a3b (prototype patch and repro test reverted).

2122.title: provider-acp silently drops agent-initiated turns (unprompted session updates, e.g. OMP async-job delivery)
2122.rootCauseOneLine: The ACP bridge forwards unprompted session/update work with no turn.open (it only opens turns for prompts it sent), so the runtime delta assembler's no-turn rule demotes every agent_message_chunk/tool_call to a thread-scoped provider/unhandled row, which the timeline hides unless showUnhandledProviderEvents is on.

prReviews.topFinding: A vouched (agent-initiated) turn is never settled when the agent process exits: removeSession clears spontaneousTurnOpen without emitting a boundary and emitSessionError skips the settling error because activePromptKind is null, so the thread hangs in 'Working...' forever (confirmed live and by a failing probe test). Also: permission requests during a vouched turn are auto-cancelled even in full mode (handlePermissionRequest gate), and the 120 s quiet window hides the last streamed message behind 'Working...' and reports 'Worked for 2m' for sub-second work.

2122.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-acp/src/bridge/bridge.ts, fold agent-initiated turns into the existing open-turn mirror (activePromptKind: 'turn' | 'compaction' | 'agent' | null) instead of a parallel boolean; in handleAgentNotification open the turn (emit ACP_TURN_STARTED_METHOD) when activePromptKind is null and the update is a work kind derived from visibility.ts's normalized kinds; settle it on every exit path: before the next turn/start or compaction (end_turn), on thread/stop interrupt (cancelled), and on agent exit/emitSessionError (emit the settling error while the turn is still marked open); treat 'agent' like 'turn' in handlePermissionRequest so full mode auto-allows and other modes forward to the user; use a 5-10 s quiet window (or a positive end signal such as a trailing usage_update, to be confirmed by recording omp acp) rather than 120 s. Bridge-local, no wire change, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
2122.caveats: No real OMP async-job session was driven (costs usage; machine has omp 16.3.10 vs the reported 17.4.0); the repro uses a scripted fake ACP agent emitting the wire shape the issue describes, run against the real bridge, real assembler, and a real dev instance. The issue's 'zero persisted events' claim is refuted on fcada5a3b: chunks persist as provider/unhandled rows that production hides (showUnhandledProviderEvents defaults to false). PR #2123 was reviewed after rebasing its commit onto fcada5a3b (one trivial import conflict). Screenshots are from a dev build, which forces unhandled rows visible; a packaged build would show nothing at all on main.

2130.title: Open file views do not refresh when a file changes on disk
2130.rootCauseOneLine: Only workspace and thread-storage previews are realtime-owned (daemon watcher -> work-status-changed/thread-storage-changed -> query invalidation, verified live); threadHostFilePreview (paths outside the workspace) refetches only on visibilitychange, projectFilePreview (New-thread view) and hostFilePreview (plugin pages) are never invalidated nor focus-refetched, and the Docs plugin's DocsFileOpener, which becomes the default .md opener once Docs is installed, reads the file once into component state with no poll/watcher/subscription/refresh control and drops a conflicting unmount save via setConflict on an unmounted component.
2130.proposedFix: (1) Make useProjectFilePreview realtime-owned: key it by the project's default environment or add a realtime-registry dirty function mapping work-status-changed to projectFilePreviewQueryKeyPrefix(projectId); at minimum switch it to RESUME_REFETCH_QUERY_POLICY. (2) For host paths, add a daemon watchPathRoot-backed subscription relayed by the server as a new change kind (bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION) that invalidates threadHostFilePreview/hostFilePreview keys; as a cheap mitigation drop useHostFilePreview's 30s staleTime and also feed window.focus into focusManager in apps/app/src/lib/query-client.ts so macOS app switches count. (3) Give plugin file openers a change signal (experimental_useFileChangeSignal or a changeToken prop derived from the owning environment/thread-storage invalidation) and have DocsFileOpener re-open the file when clean, show the existing 'Changed on disk.' banner when dirty, and render a Refresh control. (4) On a conflicting unmount save, retain the unsaved content (e.g. module-level map keyed by path, re-offered on next open) or at least toast, instead of calling setConflict on an unmounted component.
2130.caveats: Two of the issue's five surfaces are refuted: workspace-file and thread-storage previews in a thread refresh live within 3-5s (verified in an isolated headless Chrome profile; an earlier run in the shared doobie profile gave false positives because other agents' pages toggled document visibility). The issue's 'surface 2' (RESUME_REFETCH_QUERY_POLICY) actually describes useThreadHostFilePreview (absolute paths outside the workspace), which was verified stale until a visibilitychange. Surface 1 (useHostFilePreview, plugin-page right panel) was verified by code and a failing unit test only; no built-in UI path reaches it without a plugin that opens {kind:'host'} targets. The macOS app-switch claim was verified by reading query-client.ts, not on a real window. The watcher's gitignore list is computed once at watch start (a dir ignored before start is not watched; not tested). The Docs plugin is an official on-demand install, not auto-installed, so the markdown regression only affects users who installed it; once installed it is the default opener for md/mdx/markdown. The second Docs unit test asserts 'something should happen after a conflicting unmount save', which is a design expectation rather than a contract. Issue Priority/Effort project fields could not be read (token lacks read:project); issue type Bug and labels docs/ui were read via API.

2093.title: Path listing hides every dotfile and node_modules unconditionally, so file search cannot find .github/workflows/ci.yml
2093.rootCauseOneLine: The host daemon's shared recursive walker listPathsRecursively (apps/host-daemon/src/command-handlers/file-list.ts:143-145) unconditionally skips every dot-leading entry, node_modules and symlinks, with no host.list_paths/host.list_files parameter to relax it, so every server path-search route, quick-open, @-mentions and plugins inherit the rule while host.read_file serves the same files.

prReviews.topFinding: Narrowing the skip list to .git/node_modules fixes the named symptom (my repro test passes) but the uncapped per-keystroke walker now descends .venv/.turbo/.next/.cache: measured listHostPaths(query 'config') on a Python repo went from 6-8ms to 629-1234ms and the project's own config.py was pushed out of the top 8 by .venv site-packages paths; also lists dotfiles in the skill-file browser whose read path uses dotfiles:'deny' (404 on click), and the 146->147 protocol bump conflicts with main already at 150.

Does not fix #2093 (lists it as a known gap; Fixes # is blank) and must not close it. On its own: the tree RPC for host-kind files calls files.listPaths on dirname(file) with limit 10000 and the daemon walks the whole subtree before truncating, so 'Show in files' on ~/notes.md walks all of $HOME unbounded (plausible, not measured); host-kind resolution ignores experimental_hostId and throws when environmentId is null; thread-storage resolves against the server dataDir with no hostId; defaultEnabled:true + 25MB needs an explicit decision; branch 39 commits behind main.

2093.proposedFix: Separate policy from primitive: add required includeHidden: boolean, excludeNames: string[] (and respectGitignore: boolean) to hostListFilesCommandSchema/hostListPathsCommandSchema, have the daemon walker take them as arguments (always refusing to descend .git) and bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION 150->151; the server fills product defaults once (includeHidden true, excludeNames ['node_modules'], respectGitignore true) for workspace search routes and passes includeHidden:false from the two skill consumers whose read path denies dotfiles; expose includeHidden on files.listPaths/paths routes, SDK and CLI. When the root is a git worktree, produce candidates with `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` (synthesising directory entries) instead of readdir recursion so gitignored .venv/.next/.turbo/.cache vanish without a curated list while tracked .github/workflows/ci.yml appears; keep readdir as fallback for non-git roots and add a hard walk cap (e.g. 50k entries -> truncated:true). Tests: the attached repro test, a gitignored .venv not listed, .git never listed, skill listing never returns a file readProjectSkill rejects.
2093.caveats: One real codex turn ("Reply only with ok.") was spent to get a thread/environment for the UI screenshots. Benchmarks used real local repos (~/podcast, ~/browser-use, ~/mcp-client, ~/bb) on this machine; absolute timings are machine-specific but the ratios are the point. The PR #2127 host-kind unbounded-walk finding is reasoned from code (walker has no cap) and not measured because the sandbox could not read ~/Library; the PR was not exercised live as a builtin. Issue's claim about bb 0.38.0 desktop was not tested directly, but the code is unchanged since c2733ab86 so every release has it. origin/main (15f21ade7) has no change to the walker, so the bug is still present upstream.

2072.title: Plugin frontends cannot typecheck imports of BB-shimmed packages (sonner, vaul, most radix families)
2072.rootCauseOneLine: bb plugin build resolves the 21 shimmed specifiers via an esbuild onResolve filter + generated export manifest (never node_modules), while tsc uses node resolution and neither the scaffold (whose type-only devDependencies are only the shimmed packages the 4 starter components happen to import) nor the SDK's bundled .d.ts nor the docs supply declarations for 13 of them (sonner, vaul, @pierre/diffs(+/react), nine radix families).
2072.proposedFix: (1) In packages/templates/scripts/generate-plugin-scaffold.mjs, add every runtime-shimmed package (not just the starter-component subset) to the type-only devDependencies, versions mirrored from apps/app/package.json via the existing versionedDeps(); ideally move RUNTIME_SLOT_BY_SPECIFIER into a single data module shared by build-plugin-app.ts and the generator so the hand-copied SHIMMED_SPECIFIERS set (already missing @pierre/diffs) cannot drift. A prototype of this makes the repro test pass (diff in repro/). (2) Extend `bb plugin types` (syncPluginTypes in packages/templates/src/plugin-scaffold.ts) to repin those shimmed-package devDependencies to the host's versions alongside the SDK pin and report drift under --check, which also fixes the sonner 2.0.8-vs-1.7.4 mismatch `npm i -D sonner` produces today. (3) Document in bb-plugin-authoring SKILL.md, bb-guide-plugins.md and the scaffold README that shimmed packages need a devDependency for types only, at the host's version, never in dependencies. (4) Keep a guard test (the repro test, or PLUGIN_STARTER_TYPE_DEPENDENCIES ⊇ shim list). Not recommended: shipping ambient declarations from the SDK — the export manifest only has names (would be any-typed) and bundling third-party .d.ts duplicates/conflicts with copies shadcn installs.
2072.caveats: SDK 0.4.11 at base is unpublished, so the scaffold's pin was satisfied with an `npm pack` tarball of packages/plugin-sdk (the workaround the CLI itself prints); with a published SDK the steps are identical. The issue's side claim that clsx/tailwind-merge/cva land in `dependencies` was true for 0.38.0 but was already fixed by #1943 before the base commit. The claim that a `dependencies` entry "silently bloats the bundle" is refuted: the shim filter matches by specifier, dist/app.js is byte-identical (33,614 B) with sonner installed; the real cost is an unneeded install for git (--omit=dev) installs. One early `bb plugin build` ran without BB_DATA_DIR and created a toolchain cache dir under ~/.bb/plugins/ (npm package cache only); it was deleted immediately and all later builds used /tmp/bb-2072-data. No PRs are linked. The repro test file is left uncommitted in the worktree (packages/templates/test/plugin-scaffold-shim-types.test.ts).

2068.title: Archived idle threads block branch checkout after the workspace is released
2068.rootCauseOneLine: hasLiveThreadAtHostPath() (packages/db/src/data/threads.ts#L1398-L1417) filters on deleted_at IS NULL + status in starting/idle/active but never on archived_at, and archiveThread() leaves status 'idle', so an archived idle thread satisfies the branch-checkout guard in unmanagedAttachRefusal() forever and every "New branch from" thread create in that folder gets 409.

prReviews.topFinding: One-line root-cause fix (nonDeletedThreads -> liveThreads in hasLiveThreadAtHostPath) with a regression test; verified live (409 -> 201, branch bb/<thr> created) and an unarchived active/idle thread still blocks; full @bb/server (1901) and @bb/db (406) suites pass when cherry-picked onto fcada5a3b. Only low-severity notes: the new test bypasses the archive route and there is no createThreadFromRequest-level case; PR branch is a week behind main but cherry-picks cleanly.

2068.proposedFix: In packages/db/src/data/threads.ts hasLiveThreadAtHostPath, wrap the status predicate with the existing liveThreads() helper (adds archived_at IS NULL) instead of nonDeletedThreads(); keep the starting/idle/active status filter. This is exactly PR #2069. Safe because archiving an active thread synchronously moves it to 'stopping' (a status the guard already ignores) and unarchive re-applies the guard. Optional follow-ups: a route-level test via createThreadFromRequest with branch {kind:"new"}, include 'stopping' threads with a live turn in the guard, and name the blocking thread in the 409 message.
2068.caveats: Reproduced on macOS 26.5 / Node 22 rather than the reporter's Linux / Node 26 (the query is platform-independent). The live repro used two tiny real claude-code turns. The UI thread view screenshot on the PR build was taken after the thread finished, not mid-create. Worktree left on branch pr2069-on-base (PR commit cherry-picked onto fcada5a3b) with the untracked repro test file; origin/main (3 commits ahead) does not touch the guard so the bug is still present on main.

2066.title: Timeline cache retains obsolete revisions for the same request shape
2066.rootCauseOneLine: createThreadTimelineCache keys entries by `${maxSeq}|${paramsKey}`; maxSeq is monotonic so each appended event makes the prior entry unreachable but it stays in the 128-entry LRU, and the 200-row cap does not exclude ordinary streaming turns, so one viewed streaming thread fills all 128 slots with dead full responses.

prReviews.topFinding: Fix is correct and at the right layer (route-level repro goes 128 -> 1 entries; live GC'd heap growth over 100 append+refetch rounds drops from +19.4/+21.8/+21.7 MB on base to +3.6/+3.6 MB across author and revise runs, +6.0 MB in the verifier's; 695 server tests, typecheck, eslint pass; the §4a scenarios rewritten for its signature pass 2/2), but the PR description claims 'oversized replacement' coverage that does not exist in its test file, revisionKey redundantly re-embeds paramsKey (pass maxSeq as a number and delete buildThreadTimelineCacheKey instead), and it is a draft 68 commits behind main with no CI run.

2066.proposedFix: Key the response cache by paramsKey (already computed for the delta cache) and store { maxSeq, value }; a hit requires equal maxSeq, a miss deletes the slot before the row-cap check and re-inserts as MRU; delete buildThreadTimelineCacheKey and the maxSeq field of ThreadTimelineCacheKeyArgs. Implemented this revision as /tmp/bb-reports/issues/2066/repro/proposed-fix-2066.diff (timeline-cache.ts, one call site in data.ts, timeline-cache.test.ts adapted): route-level test fails before (128 !== 1) and passes after unchanged; repro-2066-unit-after-fix.test.ts passes 2/2; 25/25 timeline/delta/preview tests, turbo typecheck and eslint pass; live measurement +6.9 MB vs +21.7 MB base in the same session.
2066.caveats: Not a visual bug; no screenshots (one SVG chart of the heap measurement, now showing all eight runs). Verifier's major finding was correct and is fixed: the original §4a unit test is bound to the base string-key signature and throws TypeError against PR #2067 (confirmed by re-running on the PR branch), so the report no longer claims it passes after; signature-specific rewrites were added for the PR and for the proposed fix, and the route-level test is named as the signature-independent fail-before/pass-after evidence. measure.sh was rewritten to derive worktree/data dir/port from git and scripts/bb-dev-app status and re-run unmodified in a fresh worktree (base +21.7 MB, PR +3.6 MB, proposed fix +6.9 MB). The repro unit tests used status 'running' (not a ThreadStatus); corrected to 'active' in all three files and the base log re-captured (same 2 !== 1 / 128 !== 1 failures). Still true: the issue's '1.1-4.8 MiB response payloads' is refuted as stated (server logs eventDataBytes, input event JSON, 4.3x the response on my thread); the reporter's 300-650 MB server footprint is not shown to be dominated by this bounded ~128 x response-object waste; live repro inserts events directly into the dev SQLite DB rather than running a provider turn; RSS was not used, numbers are post-forced-GC heap via the inspector. Cleanup done: dev instance stopped, data dir and launcher logs for f02-23 deleted, ports 12532/20532/28532/9229 confirmed free, test copies removed from the worktree (branches revise-2066, pr-2067-on-base and proposed-fix-2066 remain in the worktree for review).

2062.title: ACP bridge drops model descriptions, so the model picker shows indistinguishable duplicate rows
2062.rootCauseOneLine: buildModelCatalogFromConfigOptions in plugins/provider-acp/src/bridge/model-catalog.ts#L283 hard-codes description: "" (ignoring the option.description the ACP agent sends through the passthrough schema), and the desktop ModelReasoningPicker renders only displayName with no collision disambiguation, so models sharing a display name (omp exposes 15 such collisions, e.g. github-copilot/gpt-5.1 vs openai-codex/gpt-5.1) are visually identical.

prReviews.topFinding: The bridge hunks (wire.ts description: acpOptionalString; model-catalog.ts option.description ?? "") are correct and tested, but the new MenuRowButton wrapper (flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col) inherits the <button> default text-align:center, so every model AND reasoning row in the picker becomes horizontally centered for all providers (measured labelTextAlign 'center' in the running app); additionally forwarding description for every provider makes every Claude Code / Codex row a two-line row with truncated marketing copy (popover 254px -> 321px wide, 'More models' pushed below the fold), an unannounced UI change. Recommend keeping the bridge fix and restricting desktop secondary text to label-colliding rows via the existing qualifier slot (or, if mobile parity is wanted, add text-left and call the change out).

2062.proposedFix: (1) Bridge: type `description: acpOptionalString` on acpConfigOptionSelectOptionSchema (wire.ts#L233-L238) and map `description: option.description ?? ""` in buildModelCatalogFromConfigOptions (model-catalog.ts#L283), mirroring buildModelCatalogFromSessionModels; no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed since the field is already a required string. (2) Desktop: in useThreadCreationOptions modelOptions/moreModelOptions and the ModelReasoningPicker preview mappings, detect duplicate labels and only for colliding rows set the existing `qualifier` slot (already used for Pi routeProviderId and already rendered inline + in the title tooltip) to the agent's short description or, failing that, the raw model value.
